ordered_diagnoses: Pancreatic involvement in IgG4-related disease with inflammatory bowel disease

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pancreatic syndrome with recent onset of hyperglycemia and abdominal symptoms in a patient with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular disease
salient_findings: Elevated plasma glucose and hemoglobin A1c
Swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging
key_facts: 67-year-old man with a 3-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
Managed with metformin and glimepiride
Prior percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction 2 months earlier
40-year smoking history, quit after myocardial infarction
Four episodes of bloody diarrhea daily
No abdominal pain or fever
Normal white-cell count, bilirubin, and liver function tests
Microalbuminuria of 50.7 mg/day
Anti–glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies negative
Elevated serum IgG4
Contrast-enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography showed pancreatic swelling and duct narrowing

shortlist.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and pancreatic swelling with duct narrowing

shortlist.label: IgG4-related pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and recent onset of hyperglycemia

shortlist.label: Acute pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Pancreatic swelling and elevated serum amylase and lipase

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of type 2 diabetes mellitus and pancreatic duct narrowing

shortlist.label: Pancreatic involvement in IgG4-related disease with inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4, pancreatic swelling, and history of ulcerative colitis

raw.rationale: Elevated serum IgG4 and pancreatic swelling with duct narrowing on imaging are consistent with IgG4-related pancreatitis, and the presence of extensive ulcerative colitis suggests a possible association with IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
rejected.why: While similar to IgG4-related pancreatitis, the specific diagnosis of autoimmune pancreatitis is not as strongly supported by the elevated IgG4 levels and imaging findings

rejected.label: Acute pancreatitis
rejected.why: The lack of abdominal pain and normal liver function tests do not support a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest a long-standing inflammatory process typical of chronic pancreatitis

rejected.label: Pancreatic involvement in IgG4-related disease with inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: While the patient has inflammatory bowel disease, the specific diagnosis of IgG4-related pancreatitis better explains the pancreatic findings and elevated IgG4 levels
